author: I. F. Henderson
title: Munson elected Brown County Judge, Byars wins Precinct 4 Commissioner runoff
text:
Munson elected Brown County Judge, Byars wins Precinct 4 Commissioner runoff
Tom Munson was elected Brown County Judge and Brandon Byars won the Precinct 4 County Commissioner seat in runoff elections held May 26. Munson received 2,366 votes, or 55.96 percent, defeating Patrick Howard who received 1,862 votes, or 44.04 percent.
“It’s very humbling, and all the sudden you find yourself touching 38,000-plus people with what you do,” Munson said after the final numbers were revealed. “It’s a big job, there’s a lot to be done, and I certainly appreciate the support of everybody that helped me with my campaign, that gave me words of encouragement, that voted and put up my signs. I appreciate Mr. Howard and the campaign he ran. He worked really hard and I can see that. He never gave up.”
In the March general election for county judge, Munson had received 3,001 votes (48.13 percent), while Howard had tallied 2,554 votes (40.96 percent). Incumbent County Judge Shane Britton had been suspended without pay following his arrest on five charges in November 2025; he received 680 votes (10.91 percent).
“A lot of times the winner of the primary will lose in the runoff, there’s examples even in this room, so I didn’t feel like I had it in the bag by any means,” Munson said.
Regarding his next steps as judge amid an upcoming fiscal year budget process and with Britton still suspended from office pending a decision on when he will assume duties officially as judge pro tem Joel Kelton continues to serve, “I don’t know at what point I take the position as the judge... But to the extent I’m involved it will be basically trying to understand the numbers that we have right now... so you can make good decisions on how to move forward.”
Howard responded to Tuesday's outcome by saying, “I first want to thank everyone who supported me... We worked really hard and ran really hard because of all the good things this county has given to me and my family... We stood outside until the last day even in rain until seven o’clock... We were going to fight for every vote that we could get.”
In Precinct 4's commissioner race runoff, Brandon Byars defeated incumbent Larry Traweek with Byars receiving 586 votes (51.72 percent) compared to Traweek's 547 votes (48.28 percent). "I didn’t know if I would win but I knew it would be close," Byars said after learning results.
Traweek commented, "I guess it was time for a change but I do thank everyone that did vote for me and Brandon will probably make a good one." In March's initial voting, Traweek led with 707 votes (43.51 percent), followed by Byars' tally of 554 (34.09 percent) and Doug Jester's third-place finish at 364 (22.4 percent).
A total of 4,219 ballots were cast between early voting turnout of 2,448 voters plus Election Day turnout of another 1,771 ballots—representing about sixteen-and-a-half percent participation among Brown County’s more than twenty-five thousand registered voters.
